Package net.paulhertz.pixelaudio.sampler

Class PASamplerInstrumentPool

java.lang.Object
net.paulhertz.pixelaudio.sampler.PASamplerInstrumentPool
All Implemented Interfaces:
PAPlayable, PASamplerPlayable, AudioSampleClock
public class PASamplerInstrumentPool extends Object implements PASamplerPlayable, PAPlayable, AudioSampleClock
Manages a group of PASamplerInstruments sharing the same source buffer and audio output. Provides polyphony management, buffer swapping, and per-instrument voice recycling.

Features:

  • Sample-based instruments with ADSR envelopes
  • Configurable pool size (number of instruments)
  • Configurable max voices per instrument
  • Safe buffer and sample rate propagation
  • Voice stealing via release or stop()
  • Looping detection
  • Thread-safe access

A pool handles one or more PASamplerInstrument instances. Each instrument manages a list of voices. PASamplerInstrumentPool is initialized with a poolSize and a maxVoices value, for the number of instruments and the number of voices per instrument. The total number of voices maxes out at poolSize * maxVoices. When there are no more voices to allocate, voice-stealing takes over. New lazy allocation and active/free voice lists in PASharedBufferSampler have improved voices allocation, as of version 0.9.9.2.

My suggestions for `pool size` x `max voices` settings:

  • General interactive use: 8 × 64 or 4 x 128
  • Dense curve triggering with cleaner overload behavior: 1 × 512 or 2 × 256: overload noise is fluttery, windowed
  • Greater dynamic independence: 4 × 64 or 8 × 64: overload noise is crunchy, clipped
  • Very high limits such as 16 × 256: specialized use only, with careful gain staging
YMMV, you can probably reduce these numbers without any problems.

See Issue #45 Noise in Sampler Instruments for information about suggested poolSize and maxVoices usage with PASamplerInstrumentPool.

  • Constructor Details

    • PASamplerInstrumentPool

      public PASamplerInstrumentPool(ddf.minim.MultiChannelBuffer buffer, float sampleRate, int poolSize, int perInstrumentVoices, ddf.minim.AudioOutput out, ADSRParams defaultEnv)
      Full backward-compatible constructor with a MultiChannelBuffer argument. Envelope is supplied, pitch and pan default to globalPitch and globalPan. Note that the MultiChannelBuffer we supply is not copied, we use it directly for storage. Calling applications should not modify the buffer.
      Parameters:
      buffer - shared MultiChannelBuffer
      sampleRate - nominal sample rate of the buffer (Hz)
      poolSize - number of instruments in the pool
      perInstrumentVoices - number of voices per instrument
      out - AudioOutput to patch instruments into
      defaultEnv - default ADSR envelope for all instruments

    • getCurrentSampleTime

      public long getCurrentSampleTime()
      Returns a representative sample clock from the first pooled instrument.

      All instruments are patched to the same output when the pool is constructed, but callers that need cross-engine alignment should still choose one transport clock and pass absolute sample times to every instrument.

      Specified by:
      getCurrentSampleTime in interface AudioSampleClock
      Returns:
      current sample clock, or 0 if the pool is empty
